text: # Moderation Arena — User Guide Each round shows you **one social media post** and the moderation decisions that **two different platform policies** produced for it. You compare the two decisions and tell us which one you prefer. ⚠️ Posts are sampled from real platform data and may contain graphic, sexual, violent or hateful content. --- ## 1. The post The post (text, and any images or video) appears at the top. Media is **collapsed by default** — click **▶ Show media** to expand it. For videos and posts with audio, the **audio transcript** is shown below the media. If the text or transcript is not in English, a **Translate to English** link appears under it; it opens the Google Translate website in a new tab with the text filled in. ## 2. Policy A and Policy B The same AI model (Gemma) judged the post under two different policies. Which policy is which is **hidden** (blind), and the left/right order is random. The two decisions are laid out **row by row**, Policy A on the left and Policy B on the right: | Row | What it shows | |-----|---------------| | **Label** | The DSA content category of the decision (for example *Violence*, *Cyber violence*, *Harmful speech*), or *No moderation* if the policy allows the post. A decision can have more than one category. The model's confidence is shown below. | | **Action** | The DSA restriction type the policy would apply: *Removed*, *Demoted*, *Age Restricted*, *Labeled*, *Account Restriction*, or *Send Resources* (a support measure, not a restriction) — *No action* if none | Labels and actions are named in the same way for every platform and have fixed colours, so the two decisions can be compared directly. After you have voted, **Show full policy** appears above each column and opens the complete text of that policy. It is hidden before the vote because the policy text would reveal which platform it is. ## 3. Your preference In the middle column of the **Label** and **Action** rows, choose **A**, **Both**, **Neither** or **B**. If the two policies show exactly the same label (or the same action), only **Both** and **Neither** are offered for that row. When one of the two policies is **Bluesky** there is no Action row: Bluesky is decentralised (each user chooses which actions to apply), so only the labels are compared, and Bluesky is not ranked on actions on the Leaderboard: * **Label** — which policy's label fits the post better? * **Action** — which policy's action is more appropriate? *Both* means the two are equally good, *Neither* that neither is good. When both rows are marked, click **Submit vote**. After you vote, the policies are revealed, together with the **policy quotes** each decision cited and the model's **explanation** — these are hidden until then so they do not sway your choice. **Next post** takes you to the next sample. **Skip** loads a different post without voting. ## 3b. Leaderboard **Leaderboard** in the sidebar ranks the policies from everyone's votes (**Overall**) or only yours (**Mine**). The **Label** votes and the **Action** votes are shown side by side: a rankings table (Bradley-Terry score with a 95% interval, as on the Chatbot Arena leaderboard), a head-to-head matrix and a matrix of battle counts for each. ## 4. Your name You are anonymous: there are no accounts. At the start you choose a made-up name (the 🎲 button picks one for you); it is only used to keep your votes together. Your name is asked again each time you open the page in a new tab, so it does not carry over. **Change name** in the sidebar lets you pick a different one. ## 5. Dark / light mode Use the toggle in the sidebar. Your choice is remembered in the browser.
